# Call roadmap status

Tracks the call stack roadmap in [#25](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/25). All features below are merged on `main` and shipped in **`v0.4.0`**.

| Issue | Status | Implemented behavior | Verification evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#17](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/17) | **Closed** | `canRequestCall` / `getCallDenialReason`, profile flags and session checks without ringing | Offline adapter fixtures + live read-only Telegram verification (`SELF_CALL`, peer eligibility, zero ringing RPCs) |
| [#18](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/18) | **Closed** | Folder output by peer/device, MTProto participant registry, camera/screen subscriptions, segmented WAV/MP4 and `manifest.json` | Offline multi-peer fixtures + live audio (`25.68s` WAV) & camera (`640×360` ↔ `1280×720` H.264/AAC MP4 segment rotation, `droppedFrames: 0`) |
| [#19](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/19) | **Closed** | Per-call outgoing recording override, inherited listener default, `false` to disable, path collision checks, `.webm` rejection, recovery retention, `recordingStopped` | Offline finalization tests + live outgoing video call recording (`1280×720` H.264/AAC MP4, `4.24s`, `ffprobe` verified) |
| [#20](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/20) | **Closed** | `getStreamRtmpUrl` (`revoke: false`), RTMP H.264/AAC publisher (`joinRtmp`), and separate server-selected stream viewer (`joinStreamMode`) | Offline loopback/DC fixtures + live Telegram RTMP publish (`dc5-1.rtmp.t.me`), `joinStreamMode` (`mode: 'RTMP'`, `broadcastErrors: 0`), media DC 5 `getStreamChannels` |
| [#21](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/21) | **Open** *(core live-verified)* | Native E2E conference core, subchain relay, invite link, ringing invite, participant mappings, capability-aware `sendConferenceMessage` / `conferenceMessage` (`ntgcalls` 4.x) | Offline port/simulator tests + live 2-account E2E conference (`CONNECTED`, encrypted audio heard, matching 4-emoji fingerprint `🔶🐚🚶🔋`). Removal/rekey remains blocked upstream by `ntgcalls` |
| [#22](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/22) | **Closed** | Opt-in private atomic state file (`statePath`), `flushState`, `resumeFromState` with fresh group rejoin, queue/hold and fresh recording segments | Offline two-process fixtures + live Telegram resume (fresh SSRC, preserved queue, fresh recording segment directory) |
| [#23](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/23) | **Closed** | Unwrap `confirmCall` `{ phoneCall, users }`, remove nonexistent `phone.getCall`, preserve endpoints/protocol/`customParameters`/explicit `p2pAllowed` | Offline teleproto/mtcute regressions + live outgoing P2P (`servers=2`, `CONNECTED`) |
| [#24](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/24) | **Closed** | Investigated `ntgcalls@3.0.7` (`FILE` raw only, `FFMPEG` unimplemented); documented `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` requirement + `MediaDependencyError` | Native probes + `docs/media-support.md` fallback acceptance completed |

No issue is closed solely because an offline suite passes. The independent review, final combined suite and GitHub CI status must be recorded separately in the delivery report.

## Corrections to the original diagnosis

`phone.confirmCall` returns a `phone.PhoneCall` wrapper containing `phoneCall` and `users`. The old outgoing path read the wrapper as the inner call, losing endpoints and permissions. `phone.getCall` is absent from both installed client schemas and the official MTProto schema. A slow answer was not established as the cause of the endpoint bug.

Outgoing calls already shared the listener recording setup through `startTransport`; the missing part was an explicit per-call API and reliable isolation/finalization. Native group source-change callbacks do not discover participants in the inspected binary: the new registry uses MTProto participant updates.

`sendBroadcastPart` supplies downloaded media to a native decoder. RTMP publication uses its own ffmpeg process and never uploads with that native method.

## Native and media limits

The pinned dependency is `ntgcalls@3.0.7`. Native FILE consumes raw PCM/I420; FFMPEG throws an unimplemented-encoder error. File/URL container playback requires ffmpeg. Caller-owned shell PCM does not require ffmpeg if it uses another producer. See [media support](media-support.md) for the source pins and measured decoder outputs.

Conference removal/rekey, encrypted application messages and observable cryptographic chain health are not exposed by native 3.0.7. These operations reject explicitly; there is no plaintext or custom JavaScript crypto replacement. A resolved `applyBlocks` promise and an emoji callback do not attest cryptographic conformance. The conference API is experimental until the native security and live gates are met.

State persistence stores group intent only. It does not serialize native sockets, SSRCs, P2P sessions, conference keys or RTMP keys. Restore starts the current source again and opens a fresh recording segment; it does not resume a native transport or provide gapless seeking.

## Verification contract

Run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:all`, `npm test`, and `npm run smoke` in a pinned cloud candidate. The canonical test runner discovers every `test/*.ts` entrypoint and isolates each in a fresh Node process. Media child processes must complete before native workers are created in tests that use both.

Live tests need an authorized user session and the requested peers/groups. Existing release-level live observations do not verify the changed candidate. Keep live requirements open until that candidate is exercised.


<!-- ===== docs/media-support.md ===== -->

# Media support and native decoder limits

For roadmap [#24](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/24), the supported resolution is the **ffmpeg requirement fallback**. Install `ffmpeg` for container/file/URL audio and video sources and recording/muxing; install `ffprobe` for video metadata and sizing. The `ffmpegPath` and `ffprobePath` options select the executables. Supported container/codec combinations depend on the installed ffmpeg build.

There is no verified ffmpeg-free MP4, WebM or MKV decoder exposed by ntgcalls 3.0.7. This document makes no zero-transcode or compressed-packet passthrough claim. The wrapper decodes media to raw PCM/I420; native WebRTC subsequently handles its transport and encoding.

## What the source types mean

| API/source | Actual behavior | Requirement/limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'file', path }` | `audioDescription` / `videoDescription` build native **SHELL** commands that run ffmpeg | A container readable by the installed ffmpeg build, with the requested audio/video stream |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'url', url }` | ffmpeg opens the URL and produces raw frames; separate `audioUrl` is used for audio when present | Same decoder requirement plus network access |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'shell', command }` | Caller-owned command produces raw audio | Caller must output 48 kHz stereo signed 16-bit little-endian PCM; this command need not use ffmpeg |
| Native `MediaSource.FILE` | Opens a binary file and reads raw frame-sized chunks | Headerless PCM for audio or planar I420 video matching the description; **no container demux or codec decode** |
| Native `MediaSource.FFMPEG` | Throws `FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported` | Unimplemented for input and audio output in the pinned source/runtime |
| Native `MediaSource.EXTERNAL` | Application supplies raw frames | Requires a real application decoder for compressed inputs; compressed packets are not raw frames |

`MediaSource.FILE` is the native enum, not the wrapper's `kind: 'file'`. Passing an MP4 path to native FILE and observing a resolved `setStreamSources()` promise proves only that the configuration/file was accepted. It does not show that frames were read, decoded, delivered or heard. In the probe below even a JSON file was accepted by FILE as an audio source.

No public `kind: 'media'` or generic native container source is introduced by this fallback. Example using the existing wrapper API:

```ts
await tg.join(group, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 640, height: 360, fps: 25 },
  autoLeave: false,
});
// ffmpeg -> s16le stereo PCM + yuv420p/I420 -> native WebRTC
```

## Pinned source evidence

Wrapper baseline: [`bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8`](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/tree/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8). Native dependency: **ntgcalls 3.0.7**; inspected upstream revision: [`6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557`](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/tree/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557). These are source/version pins; the installed prebuilt is identified separately by its hash below, not claimed to be a locally reproduced source build.

- [`src/media.ts` audio L10–31](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/blob/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8/src/media.ts#L10-L31) and [video L160–183](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/blob/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8/src/media.ts#L160-L183): file/URL inputs invoke ffmpeg and return `MediaSource.SHELL`. Audio is `-f s16le -ac 2 -ar 48000`; video is `-f rawvideo -pix_fmt yuv420p` with scaling and an explicit frame rate.
- [`MediaSourceFactory::from_input` L19–54](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/media_source_factory.cpp#L19-L54): FILE constructs `io::FileReader`; FFMPEG throws at L43–45. [`from_audio_output` L57–78](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/media_source_factory.cpp#L57-L78) throws the same exception for FFMPEG audio output at L72–74.
- [`FileReader` L9–45](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/io/file_reader.cpp#L9-L45): binary `ifstream`, seek and `read(size)`; no media inspection, demuxer or codec decoder. [`ThreadedReader` L27–87](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/io/threaded_reader.cpp#L27-L87) requests batches based on `sink_->frame_size()` and splits those bytes into frames.
- [`AudioSink` L9–19](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/audio_sink.cpp#L9-L19): 10 ms frames, `sample_rate * 16 / 8 / 100 * channel_count` bytes. [`AudioStreamer` L20–26](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/audio_streamer.cpp#L20-L26) sends these as 16-bit samples. The tested description uses 48 kHz stereo: 1,920 bytes per 10 ms.
- [`VideoSink` L11–22](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/video_sink.cpp#L11-L22): `width * height * 1.5` bytes per frame. [`VideoStreamer` L20–39](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/video_streamer.cpp#L20-L39) wraps those bytes as `I420ImageData`. Use even dimensions and matching frame rate. The fixture is 160×90 at 10 fps: 21,600 bytes per frame.
- [`StreamManager` L206–213](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/stream_manager.cpp#L206-L213) opens configured readers when streams start; [`handle_capture_config` L489–519](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/stream_manager.cpp#L489-L519) only opens immediately when initialized. An offline configuration acceptance is not an observed playback pass.

## Observed cloud evidence

Probe date: **2026-11-21 UTC**. Target: InstaBox `m_agq62wtsnkqjj3hlchtinfk5fi` (`tgcalls-test`), cwd `/data/home/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121`. Environment: Linux x64, Node **v22.23.3**, npm **10.9.9**, ffmpeg/ffprobe **6.1.1-3ubuntu5**. The lane clones the pinned wrapper baseline; its `node_modules` points to `/data/home/tgcalls-inspection-20261121/node_modules`, used without installation or dependency changes.

Installed native binary `@ntgcalls/linux-x64/ntgcalls.node`: **100896624 bytes**, SHA-256 `0c62cbcc0dd321719738a0678bb207f21b0743d5a0c6a8335c0a5806b44bf7f8`. Native `NTgCalls.ping()` returned `pong`. Observed runtime enums are FILE=1, SHELL=2, FFMPEG=4, EXTERNAL=32; the test imports the enums instead of inferring values from ordinal declarations.

### Native probe

A separate initial `node evidence/native-probe.mjs` run exited **0** with empty stderr:

```text
FFMPEG microphone CAPTURE -> Error: FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FILE microphone with headerless s16le fixture -> configuration resolved
FILE microphone with package.json -> configuration resolved (counterexample only)
```

The more complete media probe also observed:

```text
FILE microphone s16le stereo 48000Hz + camera I420 160x90@10 -> configuration resolved
FFMPEG microphone CAPTURE -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FFMPEG microphone PLAYBACK -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FFMPEG camera CAPTURE -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FILE microphone with compressed MP4 -> configuration resolved (NOT decode evidence)
```

These are real native calls on fresh offline P2P placeholders, each stopped afterward. There was no Telegram transport or receiving peer, so native raw playback and delivered remote frames remain unobserved.

### Representative container decode

The test generates one-second synthetic audio/video using real ffmpeg, verifies encoded codecs with ffprobe, runs the **actual wrapper audio/video command strings**, and checks non-silent signed PCM plus detailed, complete I420 frames. All subprocesses finish before constructing `NTgCalls`. This is decoder/output evidence, not a live-call test.

| Container | ffprobe-confirmed encoded codecs | Decoded PCM bytes, 48 kHz stereo s16le | Peak absolute PCM sample | Decoded I420 bytes | Frames, 160×90 at 10 fps |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MP4 | H.264 + AAC | 192512 | 2979 | 216000 | 10 |
| WebM | VP9 + Opus | 192000 | 2931 | 216000 | 10 |
| MKV | HEVC/H.265 + AAC | 196608 | 2979 | 216000 | 10 |

AAC padding/timestamps make decoded audio lengths differ; the assertions allow approximately one second and check sample alignment. A deliberately corrupt MP4 produced **exit 183**, **0 decoded bytes** with the tested ffmpeg build. The assertion requires nonzero status rather than pinning a platform-specific exit number. The research probe exited **0** with empty stderr; its missing-dependency regression was explicitly excluded and reported separately as failing, so this result is **not** a full test pass.

These outputs were also reproduced by the complete `test/media-support.ts` after it was changed to retain a dependency-guard failure until all independent media probes finish. That complete run exited **1**, never emitted `MEDIA SUPPORT PASS`, and is retained as `verify-media-support.json` / `verification.json`.

The exercised encoder choices were `libx264`, `libvpx-vp9`, `libx265`, `aac`, `libopus`. This matrix is representative, not a guarantee for every codec profile, container combination, platform, ffmpeg build or URL. Upgrade the fixtures/source investigation when changing the native dependency.

### Missing-executable regression and integration requirement

Run the complete regression separately from `npm test`:

```sh
node --import tsx test/media-support.ts
```

The baseline `package.json` only runs `test/run.ts`; adding this file alone does not put it in that command. `npm run typecheck:all` does include it and exited **0** in the cloud lane. The first complete regression run against the pinned baseline exited **1**:

```text
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception.
  at missingDependencies (.../test/media-support.ts:55:10)
```

This exposes a missing production guard, not an exempt pre-existing suite failure. The baseline receipt lists **no failing assertion exemption**. The complete regression retains a guard failure while continuing independent media evidence checks, then fails at the end; a research-only probe cannot close this regression.

Required guard behavior before passing a description to native:

- File/URL audio and video descriptions must reject a missing/non-executable `ffmpegPath` (default `ffmpeg`) with a `TgCallsError` subtype; the message identifies the executable and the `ffmpegPath` remedy. Recording commands require the same check.
- Video probing must reject a missing/non-executable `ffprobePath` with a typed error naming `ffprobePath`, rather than silently substituting default dimensions for ENOENT.
- Caller-owned shell/raw sources remain usable without ffmpeg. Resolving an executable should check PATH/file executability without spawning a child after native workers exist; this avoids introducing the known native-thread/process-spawn deadlock into every source helper.

The roadmap branch now implements these guards as `MediaDependencyError` and the complete media regression was rerun in the parent cloud worktree: `node --import tsx test/media-support.ts && npm run build && npm run typecheck:all` returned exit 0 (`media-support-green.json`). Executable discovery checks PATH and file executability without spawning. The research-phase red evidence above is retained as the regression witness. The canonical runner now discovers this entrypoint; the final combined candidate suite is still a separate gate.

One full verification pass on the isolated pinned baseline plus this lane's two artifacts returned:

| Check | Actual exit code | Scope/result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `npm run build` | 0 | Pinned wrapper source builds |
| `npm run typecheck:all` | 0 | Includes the new media-support test |
| `npm test` | 0 | Existing `test/run.ts`, `ALL TESTS PASSED`; intentional event-handler `Error: boom` fixture appears on stderr |
| `npm run smoke` | 0 | Built exports verified |
| `node --import tsx test/media-support.ts` | 1 | Container/native probes completed, missing executable guard still fails |
| `git diff --check` | 0 | Tracked patch whitespace check; the lane artifacts were new/untracked |

The overall verification command returned **1**. None of these results verifies the concurrent production changes in other lanes, a combined all-green candidate, Node 20, CI, live media, or a release.

### Reproducibility and receipts

Raw REST result envelopes and fetched pinned sources are retained locally in `/home/ocan/.hermes/cache/scratch/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121/`; cloud receipts are under `/data/home/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121/evidence/`. `evidence.json` records commands/results, pins, runtime/binary details and SHA-256 source receipts. `baseline-with-guard-test.json` preserves the original failing guard run, `research-probe.json` preserves the explicitly limited research-only run, and `source-manifest.json` pins the fetched source bytes. Generated fixtures are removed by the regression after inspection; measured output and hashes stay in the receipts.

To repeat: use the pinned dependencies, install an ffmpeg build with the listed codecs, then run the command above and `npm run typecheck:all`. Do not import this standalone test into a process that already owns native workers: it creates child processes, has a bounded deadline, and exits after stopping its own calls. A pass still requires separate authorized live playback/send/receive testing before claiming remote media support.


<!-- ===== docs/troubleshooting.md ===== -->

# Troubleshooting

## `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`

Some npm versions (seen with **npm 12 installing from a git URL**) skip `ntgcalls`'
platform-specific optional dependency. Install it yourself, matching the `ntgcalls`
version in `package.json` (currently `3.0.7`):

```bash
npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save
```

Use the matching package on other platforms:

| Platform | Package |
|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-x64` |
| Linux arm64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-arm64` |
| macOS arm64 | `@ntgcalls/darwin-arm64` |
| Windows x64 | `@ntgcalls/win32-x64` |

Installing from the npm registry (once published) resolves optional dependencies
normally and avoids this entirely. npm 10 (e.g. on many cloud images) installs the
binary correctly from a git URL.

## `default_launcher: No such file or directory (vfork_launcher)`

This confusing error from the native core almost always means **ffmpeg is not on
PATH**. ntgcalls spawns ffmpeg per source; without it you get a boost process-launch
ENOENT instead of a clear "ffmpeg not found".

```bash
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg     # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install ffmpeg             # macOS
ffmpeg -version                 # verify it resolves
```

The test suite now fails fast with a clear message if ffmpeg is missing.

## Join fails / kicked after ~25 seconds

On **UDP-blocked hosts** (some VPS/firewalls), a regular RTC join gets an ICE timeout
and Telegram kicks the participant after ~25s. Options:

- Use `joinIdle(chat, { allowCreate: true })` — creates the call in **RTMP-stream**
  mode and joins muted (no local media path needed). Existing calls are not converted.
- Presentation/screen share requires RTC and is **unavailable** in RTMP/STREAM mode.
- On UDP-capable hosts (verified on InstaBox/AWS), normal RTC joins and idle presence
  are stable indefinitely (40+ minutes tested).

Check outbound UDP:

```bash
timeout 5 bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/udp/stun.l.google.com/19302' && echo "UDP OK"
```

## `NoVoiceChatError`

There is no active voice chat in the target chat. Start one manually, or pass
`allowCreate: true` (the account needs admin rights to create a call).

## `AlreadyInCallError`

You called `join`/`joinIdle` while already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat.
`leave(chat)` first. The error carries `chatId`.

## YouTube: "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"

YouTube blocks **datacenter IPs** (cloud VMs) across all player clients. Fixes:

- **Cookies** from a logged-in browser (Netscape format):
  ```bash
  yt-dlp --cookies cookies.txt --js-runtimes node -f "bestvideo[vcodec~='^(vp09|avc1)']+bestaudio[ext=m4a]/best" URL
  ```
  Treat cookies as account credentials: store `chmod 600`, never log them, delete/rotate after use.
- A recent **yt-dlp** and a JS runtime (`--js-runtimes node` or deno) — extraction
  without a JS runtime is deprecated and may miss formats.
- Prefer `vp9`/`avc1` over AV1 for video (AV1 is too heavy to decode in real time on small VPS).
- Fallback: download from a residential IP, then transfer the file to the cloud host.

## Login / 2FA (teleproto)

- `client.start()` probes `updates.getState()`, which throws `AUTH_KEY_UNREGISTERED`
  on an empty session. For QR login use `client.signInUserWithQrCode(...)` directly;
  the QR token is a Buffer — encode `tg://login?token=<base64url>` for the QR image.
- For phone login, provide `phoneNumber`, `phoneCode`, and `password` (2FA) callbacks.
- Keep the resulting StringSession secret; reuse it with `new StringSession(str)` +
  `client.connect()`.

## Process aborts on exit

`process.exit()` immediately after native use can abort during WebRTC teardown
(cosmetic). `await tg.dispose()` and let queued callbacks drain before exiting;
long-running bots are unaffected.

## Mixing `telegram` and `teleproto`

Pass the matching `Api` namespace to each `TgCallsClient` to avoid ambiguous TL
auto-detection. mtcute uses its own TL schema and needs no `Api`.

## Incoming P2P call never connects (ICE `TIMEOUT`)

Four distinct failures can each stop a 1-on-1 call; the wrapper fixes them, but
they matter if you call `ntgcalls` directly or debug a fork:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `An array was expected` from `initExchange` | `bytes::binary` is read as `Napi::Array` — `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` are rejected | pass `Array.from(buf)` |
| `phone.acceptCall` → `CALL_PEER_INVALID` | TL `long` is a `big-integer` object; `BigInt(obj)` goes through `Number` and loses precision | convert via `toString()` |
| `connectP2p` → `incomplete JSON [boost.json:3]` | `customParameters: ''` is a *present* optional; `json::parse("")` throws | pass `'{}'` |
| `Failed to parse received SCTP packet`, `Sorting 0 available connections`, then `TIMEOUT` | versions list includes `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` → ntgcalls routes signaling over an SCTP data channel, but Telegram sends it via MTProto | restrict to `8.0.0`/`9.0.0` |

Debug with `setLogLevel(LogLevel.DEBUG)` (from `ntgcalls`) and
`listenCalls({ debug: true })`. A healthy call logs, in order:
`Using signaling V2 Legacy` → `Decrypting packets` (inbound signaling) →
`new remote candidate` → `state= 2` (`CONNECTED`) →
`First audio RTP packet sent to pacer`.

## mtcute: no `INCOMING`, calls do nothing

Two mtcute-specific traps. Both are silent — no error is thrown.

1. **`client.connect()` does not start the updates loop.** `onRawUpdate` is
   emitted from that loop, so with `connect()` only outgoing RPCs work; no
   `updatePhoneCall` ever reaches the library. Use `client.start()` (it connects
   *and* launches the loop). Symptom: the call rings on the phone, the listener
   logs nothing at all.
2. **mtcute objects use `_`, GramJS/teleproto use `className`.** Fixed in the
   library (`kind` is normalised from either), but any custom adapter must do the
   same: `phoneCallRequested` vs `PhoneCallRequested`.

Verify the loop independently of calls:

```ts
client.onRawUpdate.add((u) => console.log('RAW', (u?.update ?? u)?._));
await client.sendText('me', 'self-test'); // must log RAW updateMessageID
```

Session note: a GramJS/teleproto string session can be reused with mtcute via
`@mtcute/convert` (`convertFromGramjsSession`) + `client.importSession()`.

## Outgoing call: ICE `TIMEOUT` (state 8) right after the peer answers

`phone.confirmCall` returns a wrapper `{phoneCall, users}`. Reading `connections` from the wrapper instead of `phoneCall` loses the server list and peer permission flags. The roadmap branch unwraps this response and passes the inner endpoints, protocol and custom JSON to native. Direct P2P is allowed only when `p2pAllowed === true`.

`phone.getCall` is absent from both installed client schemas and the official MTProto schema. It is not a fallback for this shape error. There is no established evidence that slow answering caused the missing endpoints. If a current call still fails, inspect the confirmed inner call and fresh native/signaling logs rather than adding a nonexistent RPC.


<!-- ===== AGENTS.md ===== -->

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working on **tgcalls-js**.

## What this is

A TypeScript wrapper (`src/`) around the `ntgcalls` native binding that streams
audio/video into Telegram voice chats via a GramJS-family or mtcute MTProto client.
ESM (`"type": "module"`), strict TypeScript, Node ≥ 18.

## Commands

```bash
npm install            # npm 11+ may warn "install scripts blocked" for esbuild — cosmetic
npm run build          # tsc → dist/
npm run typecheck:all  # tsc -p tsconfig.all.json (src + examples + test)
npm test               # node test/all.mjs — every test/*.ts in isolated processes, NO credentials
npm run smoke          # node smoke.mjs — verify dist/index.js exports
```

CI without GitHub Actions: `scripts/ci.sh` (npm ci → build → typecheck:all → test →
smoke; `--fresh [ref]` clones pristine first). GitHub Actions may be disabled at the
account level — prefer `scripts/ci.sh` for verification.

## Hard rules

- **Never run live joins without an explicit user-account session and permission.**
  Bots cannot join voice chats. The offline test suite is the default verification path.
- The offline suite uses a **fake MTProto client + the real ntgcalls native core** — it
  proves protocol plumbing (ssrc round-trip, cleanup, races, dispose) without login.
- `ffmpeg` must be on PATH to run `npm test`; the suite fails fast with a clear message
  if it is missing.

## Native binary pitfall

`npm install` from a git URL on some npm versions (e.g. npm 12) skips the optional
`@ntgcalls/linux-x64` package → `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`.
Fix: `npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save` (match the `ntgcalls` version).

## Domain pitfalls (do not regress these)

- Join order is fixed: getFullChannel → createCall → setStreamSources → joinGroupCall
  → connect. The same join-params string goes to JoinGroupCall; its ssrc is reused for
  LeaveGroupCall.
- `setStreamSources` REPLACES all devices — omitting the video channel drops it.
  `setSource()` must rebuild video. Camera and screen cannot be active simultaneously.
- `streamEnd` fires once per playback; with video, wait for BOTH audio and video to end
  before auto-leave.
- A failed join must stop the native call and send LeaveGroupCall (no zombie participant).
- mtcute TL `Long` (low/high) objects must be preserved by reference — do not convert to
  bigint. GramJS/teleproto use plain bigint.
- `ConnectionState` is numeric (CONNECTING=1, CONNECTED=2, FAILED=4, TIMEOUT=8, CLOSED=16).
- On native CLOSED/FAILED, leave via MTProto BEFORE notifying listeners.

## Conventions

- Library errors extend `TgCallsError` (`src/errors.ts`); add new typed errors there.
- Internal warnings go through `opts.logger` (default `console.error`) — do not
  `console.log` directly from library code.
- Public API is re-exported from `src/index.ts`; keep `src/types.ts` the source of truth
  for shared types. Examples live in `examples/`, tests in `test/`.
- Examples use `teleproto` (the maintained GramJS fork); runtime still supports `telegram`.
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`. Keep them in sync with the
  public API when you change signatures. `llms-full.txt` is generated from the
  sources declared in `scripts/generate-docs.py`: run `python3 scripts/generate-docs.py`
  and verify with `python3 scripts/generate-docs.py --check`.

## Release

Version in `package.json` + a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Tag `vX.Y.Z` and
`gh release create vX.Y.Z` (releases via gh API work even when Actions is disabled).


<!-- ===== CHANGELOG.md ===== -->

# Changelog

## 0.4.0 (2026-11-24)

- **Gemini Multimodal Live Voice & Video AI Bridge (`connectGeminiLive`):** built-in WebSocket `BidiGenerateContent` session (`GeminiLiveSession`) connecting group voice chats, 1-on-1 P2P calls, and E2E conferences directly to Google's Gemini Live API (`models/gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest`), with automatic `48 kHz ↔ 16 kHz / 24 kHz` PCM resampling, real-time input/output audio transcription, thought separation (`onThoughtOutput`), instant barge-in interruption, and optional multimodal video frame forwarding (`i420ToBmp`) — verified live over Telegram 1-on-1 P2P voice call.
- **Voice AI External Frame Bridge (`{ kind: 'external' }`):** zero-`ffmpeg` `MediaSource.EXTERNAL` capture & playback across group calls, P2P calls, and conferences (`onAudioFrame`, `onVideoFrame`, `pushAudioFrame` with auto-10ms slicing & paced queue, `pushVideoFrame`, `interruptAudio`, `onVoiceActivity` VAD, `resamplePcmS16le`, `computePcmRms`, `i420ToBmp`).
- **Playback Filters, Advanced Queue & Voice Chat Admin RPCs:**
  - `seek()`, `setVolume()` (0–200%), `setSpeed()` (0.5–2.0×), `setLoop('off' | 'one' | 'all')`, and `setAudioFilter()` (`'bassboost'`, `'nightcore'`, `'vaporwave'`, `'8d'`, `'karaoke'`, `'treble'`, `'normalizer'`, `'echo'`, or `{ custom }`).
  - `playNext()`, `removeQueueTrack()`, `moveQueueTrack()`, `shuffleQueue()`, and `idleTimeoutMs` auto-leave timer.
  - `joinAs` channel/alias support, `getParticipants()`, `editParticipant()`, `setRaiseHand()`, `muteParticipant()`, `setParticipantVolume()`, `setCallTitle()`, `endGroupCall()`, `exportCallInvite()`, and `toggleNativeRecording()`.
- **Call preflight without ringing (#17):** `canRequestCall()` and `getCallDenialReason()` via `users.getFullUser` and session checks on both GramJS/teleproto and mtcute adapters (verified live).
- **Per-participant folder recording (#18):** `startRecording(chat, { dir, video })`, `ParticipantRegistry`, `GroupParticipantController`, `FolderRecorder`, MTProto participant pagination/delta/min-field merge cache, attributed `remoteSourceChange` (`origin: 'mtproto'`), and `manifest.json` (verified live).
- **Outgoing P2P recording & finalization (#19, #23):** per-call `OutgoingCallOptions.record` override, active path collision guards, H.264/AAC MP4 muxing, `confirmCall` `phone.PhoneCall` unwrap, and `recordingStopped` / `recordingError` events (verified live: `1280×720` H.264/AAC MP4).
- **RTMP publisher & broadcast stream viewer (#20):** `getStreamRtmpUrl()` (`revoke: false`), `joinRtmp()` (`RtmpPublisher`), and `joinStreamMode()` (`BroadcastController`) with explicit media-DC routing (verified live on Telegram RTMP ingest & DC 5).
- **Experimental E2E conference core (#21):** `createConference()`, `joinConference()`, `exportConferenceInvite()`, `inviteConferenceParticipants()`, `getEmojiFingerprint()`, `leaveConference()`, and capability-aware `sendConferenceMessage()` / `conferenceMessage` for `ntgcalls >= 4.0.0-alpha03` (2-account live E2E audio + matching 4-emoji fingerprint verified).
- **Opt-in state persistence & fresh resume (#22):** `statePath`, `flushState()`, and `resumeFromState()` with atomic writes, fresh group rejoin/SSRC allocation, playlist restore, and fresh recording segment directories (verified live).
- **Media requirements (#24):** documented `ntgcalls@3.0.7` `FILE`/`FFMPEG` limits and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` requirements in `docs/media-support.md`; added `MediaDependencyError`.

## 0.3.0 (2026-11-20)

- **1-on-1 P2P voice & video calls (incoming & outgoing) — verified live** on both `teleproto`/GramJS and `@mtcute/node`:
  - `listenCalls({ source, video?, record?, autoAccept?, onIncoming?, debug? })`, `callUser(userId, { video?, record? })`, `stopListeningCalls()`, `activeCallPeers()`, and `getEmojiFingerprint()`.
  - Automatic plain-JS-array conversion (`jsBytes()`) across the `ntgcalls` N-API `bytes::binary` boundary (`initExchange`, `exchangeKeys`, `sendSignalingData`, `RTCServer.peerTag`).
  - V2 external MTProto signaling (`8.0.0`/`9.0.0`) negotiation, lossless 64-bit TL `accessHash` handling (`asBigInt0()`), and `ConnectionState.CLOSED` (`16`) emission on peer teardown.
  - Multi-handler event subscription (`on`, `off`, `once`) with unsubscribe callbacks and isolated error handling.

## 0.2.0 (2026-11-19)

- **Built-in playlist & queue:** `play()`, `enqueue()` / `then()`, `skip()`, `playOnHold()`, `clearQueue()`, `getCurrent()`, and `getQueue()` with automatic track advancement and hold-loop fallback.
- **Incoming call audio recording:** `startRecording(chat, path, opts?)`, `stopRecording(chat)`, `getRecording(chat)`, and `isRecording(chat)` mixing remote speakers natively via `ntgcalls` into `ffmpeg` (`.wav`, `.mp3`, `.opus`).

## 0.1.0 (2026-11-18)

- **Core group voice, video & screen-share SDK:**
  - `join()`, `joinYouTube()`, `joinIdle()`, `setSource()`, `startPresentation()`, `stopPresentation()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `mute()`, `unmute()`, `leave()`, `time()`, and `dispose()`.
  - Dual MTProto adapter support (`GramjsAdapter` for `teleproto` / `telegram` and `MtcuteAdapter` for `@mtcute/node`) with automatic client detection.
  - High-resolution split video+audio stream resolution (`resolveYouTubeStreams()`, `VideoQuality` presets `360p`–`4K`), typed errors (`TgCallsError`, `AlreadyInCallError`, `NoVoiceChatError`, `UnrecognizedClientError`), and configurable `logger`.
